Cook Public Library programs per the library's monthly newsletter (November 2026). Recurring items (rodeo, commissioners, ghost walk, Lions Club meetings on the 2nd and 4th Tuesdays) show the next occurrence. Warren County Park District events page SUSPENDED as a source per Cap'n (2026-10-03): it sits behind a Cloudflare bot challenge (403 since 2026-09-24). Do not fetch it or report it as failing; its items from the 2026-09-23 check are kept until they expire. Resume only when Cap'n provides a working source. Event notes and dateLabels are shown to readers: write them for readers (what, when, where, and a helpful pointer like "check the event website for times" when a detail is missing). Never put editorial or process notes in them ("not published", "confirm before printing", "corrected from", "checked on"); record corrections in the commit message instead. Tag Christmas-season community events (tree lightings, Santa visits, holiday markets, single-date light shows) with "holiday" so they also appear on the Holiday Lights guide. Waynesville area vs. regional: an event counts as Waynesville-area when its venue names Waynesville, Corwin, Harveysburg, Oregonia, Ridgeville, Lytle, Mount Holly, Crosswick, Caesar Creek or ZIP 45068/45054/45065 (see src/lib/events.js); always put the town in the venue. Optional "cost" (e.g. "Free", "$5 adults, kids free") and "accessibility" (e.g. "Wheelchair accessible; parking behind the building") show as a line under the event, only when the organizer or its source says so. Set "local": true or false to override (e.g. an online survey about Waynesville, or an out-of-town group serving Waynesville families). Optional "orgs": ["<exact name from churches.json>"] ties an event to a church on the Churches page when its venue doesn't name the church.

items.title: Waynesville Fantasy Festival
items.venue: Downtown Waynesville
items.note: Third annual free, family-friendly fantasy festival downtown. On High Street: LARP Shire archery, training grounds, a hoedown and dance-off; the Nartum Kaal orc tribe; Sage Fire fire performance and photo op; Midwest Falconry falcon encounters; and live music from Shane the Bard. The Dwarven Beer Garden by the Village Restaurant has DORA beverages and live music at the Villager Pub tent, a potion bar and craft vendors, with Sean Nos at 11 AM and 5 PM and Creep It Real at 12:30 and 3:30 PM; a Whiskey Witches bourbon tasting is at 5 PM inside the Villager Pub (preregistration required). Riddles in the Dark is at 3 PM at the Stone House Tavern. Food trucks: 1572 Roadhouse BBQ, 513 Bubble Tea, The Naughty Lobstah, Graze and Go, Nothing Bundt Cakes and All American Griddle. Tap Details for the festival map, with restrooms and vendor locations.

items.title: Playoff football, Region 20 semifinal: Waynesville at Graham
items.venue: Graham High School, 7800 W. State Route 36, St. Paris (away)
items.note: Division V, Region 20 semifinal. Waynesville (9-2) beat Preble Shawnee in Round 2 and travels to Graham in St. Paris. Per the Spartans' game-day flyer: buy tickets online through OHSAA's Hometown Ticketing (same price as the gate); the gate takes cash only, no cards. Visitors should park in the gravel lot past the school's main entrance, closest to the visitor stands. The high school student spirit bus leaves at 5:15 PM (permission slip required; $5 student tickets online). Can't make the trip? Graham streams the game on HUDL for a fee. Tap Details for the flyer.
